model_dependencies.unpinned: unpinned: no model version was requested. dna_client.create(api_key) and create(api_key, timeout=300) leave model_version None, so every ScoreVariantRequest carried an empty model_version and the server chose. No response message carries a model version (model_version is a request field only in dna_model_service.proto) and no cache file, result or job log records one, so which model answered cannot be established from disk

registration.lift_check: the lifted function, handed chr21's 446 UNKNOWN blocks and unknown_scoring's predicate (names a coding gene), must reproduce 7f7c8c1 to the digit: 22,200 windows drawn, 2 undrawable, 16,706 carrying an element, 10,908 naming; 285 blocks carrying an element, 140 naming. Any difference means the lift is wrong and no genome-wide figure is reported
registration.reproduce_exactly: every field this script already wrote on 2026-09-16 (real_unknown 331 of 531 blocks with an element move, 0.6234; moves per element 0.2476; the other tiers; by case; the length deciles; 331 named blocks with their targets): the tables are unchanged and the window reading cannot change a yes or no (see scripts/onetarget_consumers.py)
registration.primary: real unknown (882 blocks, copies out), the script's own question: does a block carrying a scored element carry one that moves a gene. Against 50 windows per block of the block's length, drawn inside the chromosome's scored-element span and rejected on overlap with any organiser block, pooled over the 24 chromosomes

readings.below_chance: block rate more than 5.0 points below the random rate: a lead at a real-unknown block is rarer than at random sequence of the same length outside unknown space. Registered as a live possibility and as the expected one (chr21, coding targets: 49.1% against 65.3%), not as a failure: it says what the 331 leads are worth
readings.at_chance: within 5.0 points: a lead carries no block-level information
readings.above_chance: more than 5.0 points above: the first above-chance reading of the leads

secondary: the same control with 'names a coding gene' as the question, the chr21 instrument's
the neutral tier as a second target set, since it is the script's own comparison
the window reading's genes at the bar per block, beside the head gene per element
registration.caveat: the random windows avoid all UNKNOWN space, so 'chance' is sequence outside it of the same length, which is gene-richer than the unknown; the tier comparison inside length deciles stays the within-unknown control

reading: 331 real-unknown blocks carrying a scored element carry one that moves a gene (62.3%), against 86.0% of length-matched random windows outside the organiser's blocks (-23.70 points), which reads below chance: a lead at a real-unknown block is rarer than at random sequence of the same length outside unknown space. A named target here is a lead, not a finding; the random windows sample gene-richer sequence than the unknown, so the tier comparison inside length deciles stays the within-unknown control
